chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Aftermath: Lewis as musical director and Monte Kay's money
summary: Milt Jackson later said the group only started making money after Kay left; Clarke says he was shut out of writing and simply says he wanted to bash.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: That's right. He went for that, and that's what made me so -- I was like -- I couldn't believe it. I said, "No, this is not possible." But that's the way it was. So I saw Milt there, you know, was it the month of -- June, he was here. So he says, "After 20 years I finally got out of there." He says, "The only thing I have against you is you didn't take me when you left."

You know? Because Monte wound up stealing their money, like I knew he would, and Bags said, "I wonder if something's funny." He said, "After we broke up we started making $5,000.00 a concert." He said, "But before we never made that kind of money." He says, "Man, we hardly made anything." So I said, "I knew it would be that way." He let Monte Kaye in at 20 percent, I knew it was the end. That was the end, because John Lewis was writing the music, which he was getting royalties from all those albums we made, plus film music and all that. And I used to say, "Well, let Bags. Bags writes nice tunes. I write tunes. Let us all write." "No. I'm the musical director, now, if you guys want to put up with me, I'm the musical director and that's the way it is." So then that's when I -- in Frisco he started talking like that. So I said, well, this is no place for me. I'm getting out of here. You know, before something drastic happens and you really lose friendship with people.
So before that all comes, while he still speaks and hugs me and kisses me and all that John does, you know, but I feel back in my head that it's not kosher.

But you know, anyway, I tolerated the whole thing, and like nothing ever happened. And people will say, 'Why did you leave the Modern Jazz Quartet?' I say, 'Well, you know how I like to play, I like to bash, and they stopped bashing, so I left.' I try to bring it down as simple as I can, you know.
Yeah. Well, as a matter of fact, Kenny, you'd have never kept it up anyway, would you?
No. I couldn't. No, no, not 20 years.
